name: Pennsylvania

windshield.strip: Table X: windshield 70% (factory tint per FMVSS 205)

frontSide.note: Table X (inspection regulation). The statute itself (4524(e)) only bars material that does not permit a person to see inside through the windshield, side wing or side window; Commonwealth v. Brubaker (Pa. Super. 2010) held the 70% regulation is not incorporated into 4524(e)(1)

rear.note: Table X: 70% for 1998 and newer passenger cars; pre-1998 cars: VESC-20 labelled material; a treated rear window requires mirrors per § 175.264

backSide.note: Table X: trucks and multipurpose passenger vehicles - no requirement

tint.measuredHow: not stated; Table X says levels 'assume a 3% accuracy (±3%)'

tolerance.cite: 67 Pa. Code ch. 175, Table X ('All light transmittance levels listed below assume a 3% accuracy (±3%)')

tint.dualMirrors: Required (per § 175.264) if the rear window is treated
tint.certificateOrSticker: PennDOT certificate of exemption (medical or pre-1984) must be carried and shown to police and at inspection

medicalExemption.text: PennDOT certificate of exemption for the owner or a household member who regularly drives/is driven, for a condition approved with the Medical Advisory Board, certified by a licensed physician or optometrist; the regulation limits medical exemptions to colorless (UV-filtering) material; void on sale/transfer

penalty.text: Summary offense; fine amount for 4524(e) not stated in the section read

quotes: No person shall drive any motor vehicle with any sun screening device or other material which does not permit a person to see or view the inside of the vehicle through the windshield, side wing or side window of the vehicle.
Trucks & Multi-Purpose Passenger Vehicles 70% 70% No Requirement No Requirement
All light transmittance levels listed below assume a 3% accuracy (±3%).
An application for a certificate of exemption will be granted only for colorless sun screening device or other material

helmet.conditions: Helmet optional for riders 21+ licensed at least two full calendar years or who completed an approved safety course; passengers 21+ of an exempt operator also exempt; eye protection required for all

handheldPhone.fineText: Paul Miller's Law (Act 18 of 2024, effective June 5, 2025): handheld use $50 summary offense; written warnings only during the first 12 months (to about June 5, 2026); texting also $50 (3316)

studdedTires.season: Nov 1 - Apr 15 (max 2/32 in. projection; Governor may extend by executive order)

radarDetector.note: No state ban found; commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

openQuestions: Numeric 70% limits come from the inspection regulation (Table X), not the statute; courts have held the statute only requires that one can see inside
Exact start of the 3316.1 fine period inferred from 'eff. 12 months' after June 5, 2024 plus a 12-month warning period
Lift/suspension limits in 67 Pa. Code ch. 175 not read; underglow not located
